obligations.assertion: - The protected bytes encode exactly `{1: -19, 4: kid}`. `kid` is a byte string containing the exact 72 ASCII bytes of the existing derived signer ID. Unprotected headers must be the empty map. No unknown header, duplicate key, `crit`, content type or algorithm alias is accepted. This closed subset is a local restriction, not a general COSE reader. Header names and tag semantics follow [RFC 9052](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9052.html).

Tenant/scope, request and episode IDs are signed because they are in `c`.

obligations.assertion: Full-payload COSE is chosen to avoid inventing an ambiguous digest-payload wrapper. It differs from the proposed canonical spec's raw-digest signing equation and must be ratified explicitly. An old 64-byte signature cannot be inserted into this container and become a valid COSE signature. A later hash-envelope profile would need its own specification and vectors, not a flag in P1.

obligations.owner: ABI schema owner and independent cryptographic reviewer
obligations.assertion: `parse_p1(container: &[u8], payload: &[u8], limits: CryptoLimits) -> Result<ParsedP1, ProfileError>` checks bounds before ownership/allocation. Container cap 256 bytes; protected cap 128 bytes; kid exactly 72; signature exactly 64; payload cap 1,048,576 bytes. Container reader permits only the single outer tag and expected structure, definite lengths, shortest argument encodings, ascending canonical integer header keys, no trailing bytes or duplicate maps. Container depth at most 3 excluding the separately parsed protected map; protected map exactly two entries, no nesting. It must not relax the existing generic reader's tag ban: peel/check tag in the dedicated bounded envelope parser and use existing canonical machinery only where compatible. RFC 8949 distinguishes basic validity from deterministic encodings; this profile deliberately requires deterministic bytes. [RFC 8949 §§3.2, 4.2, 5.6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8949.html)

obligations.assertion: AdmissionContext also names the expected payload/container digests, profile/domain/version/contract, namespace and signer. Admission requires equality with every corresponding report binding, including tenant/scope and request/episode IDs, before consulting grants. Any mismatch yields static `VerificationBindingMismatch`. The candidate admitted bytes must be the immutable bytes owned by the report, never another buffer selected by context. Current grants resolve in that same namespace for the report's signer and payload scope; an earlier key snapshot is verification provenance, not current authorization. An admission decision binds these same identities plus the current trust/policy/consent and writer revisions; commit rechecks them. Authenticated actor claims must satisfy owner policy for this payload, rather than merely agree with an unsigned context.

obligations.assertion: `apply_trust_command(command: TrustCommand, auth: AdminAuthorization, expected_revision: u64) -> Result<TrustCommandResult, TrustError>` is a separately authorized local operation. Commands are Register, Activate, Retire, Revoke, and atomic Rotate; proof of possession is separate from permission to administer. `TrustCommandResult` distinguishes `Applied(receipt)` from `HistoricalReplay(receipt)`; a receipt names the original resulting revision and command digest, not a current key disposition. No command executes in this design. Proposed wire/receipt forms must stay private until ABI agreement.
